items.title: Carolyn Buck Interview, 1969-03-25
items.q: I take him into his doctor's office. We had a doctor's visit that morning.

ctx.x: You were there the night that he played his last job. Did he send at that time? I mean, did he maybe sense that that was the last time he was going to play anything? Or not?

Well, every night he played, he sensed it might be his last. But that night was extra special for one reason. I take him into his doctor's office. We had a doctor's visit that morning. Friday morning. And he had complained of a scratchy throat. And the first thing the doctor examined him, he says, Get home and get to bed. Now. And George very teasingly said, I'm working tonight. And Dr. Harmon says, Oh no, you're not. And he said, Oh yes, I am. And this went on. So when the doctor left out of the room, he says,…
Yes, I was there at the end. He was trying to play really well. I don't know. He was.
